text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITICAL NEWS RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski will not approve the dismissal of Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz advanced by the deputies of the co-ruling Polish Peasants Party (PSL) as a result of a cabinet dispute on advance harvest payments to be paid to farmers, Kwasniewski's spokesman Antoni Styrczula said.
- Solidarity trade unions will sue the ex-communist Trybuna daily for accusations of delaying government aid to flood victims.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Dutch KTI firm will install equipment to produce lead-free low-benzene fuel at Poland's biggest refinery Petrochemia Plock.
The new facilities' annual output capacity will be 700,000 tonnes, the refinery said.
- Poland's car makers will not push up prices by the end of August, the companies said.
Some imported car dealers have already increased prices due to changing currency exchange rates.

- According to opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) deputy Bogdan Borusewicz, the ailing Stocznia Polnocna shipyard in Gdansk will probably close down in a month's time due to alleged fund mismanagement by the yard's board.
The shipyard will not be closed down this year, the yard's president Wojciech Macieja said.
In the first six months of 1997 the plant made a net profit of 1.5 million zlotys, Macieja said.

- Poland's government and the European Commission on Wednesday will sign an agreement on PHARE funding of 64.6 million European Currency Units (ECU) to finance reconstruction following floods in southern Poland, Poland's European Integration Committee (KIE) secretary Danuta Hubner said.

- Poland's hard currency reserves which now reach $19.7 billion will be invested in treasury securities issued by other countries, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank's deputy president, Krzysztof Barburski said.
Despite some earlier plans, the funds will not be used to underwrite long-term credits by Polish exporters, Barburski said.

- The Bank of America will organise and underwrite investment credit for the national power grid (PSE) to build a new power and heating plant in Nowa Sarzyna, Rzeszow province, worth $117 million to be carried out in the next 17 years, the bank said.
- NBP has given the green light to the appointment of Dong Chang Park as president of LG Petro Bank in Lodz, central Poland.
- The Jupol firm of Bytom will construct a car tyre recycling plant worth 9 million zlotys at the site of the bankrupt Huta Bobrek steel mill, the company said.
The new plant will recycle up to 15,000 tonnes of tyres.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's cabinet has produced an anti-dumping bill in agreement with the standards of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
- The Dutch Philips electronics maker will supply 500,000 decoders to a new satellite television service to be launched in Poland, Philips said.
- Poland's Polstar Records music firm has signed a long-term licensing agreement with Britain's V2 Music.
- Bank Czestochowa plans to increase its share capital by 1.5 million zlotys through an issue of between 2,500 and 13,000 shares, the bank said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's treasury ministry is seeking an adviser to sell up to 15 percent of the Pekao SA banking group in a public offering, the ministry said.
PARKIET
- The net loss of the listed Swarzedz furniture maker reached 2.4 million zlotys in July as a result of a previously planned break in production, the company said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
